input.quote: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
input.rationale: Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) addresses only access wind-down, Deliverable delivery and Fee refunds. Section 10.1 refers to "any agreed transition period" but creates no transition-assistance obligation or period, and no provision anywhere obliges Vendor to return or export Customer Data in a usable format or to certify deletion: Section 16.5 covers only Confidential Information and expressly defers Customer Data to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist in the Agreement and Section 15 contains only processing-limitation and privacy-compliance terms. The rule's material elements (transition assistance period and data return within 30 days) therefore fail even the fallback, and the missing return obligation leaves us exposed to the walk-away scenario of no data return. Inserted new Section 10.3 at the preferred position (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day machine-readable return, certified deletion), with 90 days offered as a fallback in the comment.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or an Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for extraction all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject only to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an exit clause: on termination we need up to six months of transition assistance at your then-current rates, return of our Customer Data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion afterwards. The current Section 10 covers access wind-down and Deliverables but says nothing about getting our data back or migration help; if six months is difficult we can work with 90 days of assistance.
proposal.summary: Insert Section 10.3 requiring transition assistance, Customer Data return within 30 days, and certified deletion.
